target_customer: Nursing homes and memory care facilities (mainly Dutch, later US and Canadian) that buy bed sensors plus an app subscription for nursing staff
problem: Nursing homes are short of staff and rely on walkie-talkies and sensors with many false alarms, so night shifts are stressful and falls and bedsores happen.
business_model: Hardware sensor plus B2B SaaS subscription per bed
product_category: IoT bed sensor and care-team app for elderly care

founders.name: Menno Gravemaker
founders.background_notes: YC page bio: sold candles as a child, later worked many evening and night shifts in a nursing home while his grandmother lived there and saw the false alarm problem. Education and employers not stated on the pages opened.

investors: Centre for Aging + Brain Health Innovation

technical_complexity.rationale: A small team had to build a sensor plate that sits under mattresses, wireless connectivity and an app that predicts bed exits; the company later claims a bed exit can be flagged up to 70 seconds early, which is a company claim.

defensibility.rationale: Hardware installed under every bed and workflow integration with care staff create some lock-in, but bed pressure sensors as a category were already common.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source found showing an incumbent copying or buying it by 2024; the company raised its largest reported round in September 2024.

market_need_then: Staff shortages in nursing homes and high false alarm rates in existing sensors, stated by the company; Vilans is cited by a profile as estimating hours saved per day for a 90-resident home.

identity.voice_and_tone: calm and reassuring, tagline 'A calmer workflow for personalized care', question-style product copy

brand_strength.rationale: Company site is calm and consistent in three languages, but no press about the brand itself or community was found.

outcome_analysis: Momo Medical is still operating and raised a reported 6.5 million euro round led by the pension fund investor PGGM in September 2024, years after YC Summer 2021. Its founder had direct nursing home night shift experience, which fits the pain it targets. The company has reached many Dutch care organizations and now lists offices abroad, but the funding history before 2024 and revenue are not public in sources found.
notes: Round amount is 6.5 million euros; no USD figure is stated by sources so amount_usd is null. Series A label comes from a law firm headline seen in search results (Polsinelli) and an aggregator, not opened. Aggregators give conflicting totals ($7.3M to $8.9M) and a founding year of 2017 or 2018. A 500K euro ERDF grant is mentioned in the Silicon Canals article without a date. A search snippet says co-founder Ide Swager, Delft alumni, and an early 2020 pivot from pressure ulcers to broader nursing home use; those were not confirmed on an opened page. Competitor search found only undated aggregator lists (EarlySense, Oxevision), so the list is left empty. Outcome search found no acquisition, shutdown or layoffs.
